parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
A progressive longitudinal wave travels through a medium from left to right. Fig. 4.1 shows
the positions of some of the particles of the medium at time t_{0} and a graph showing the
particle displacements at the same time t_{0}.
Particle displacements to the right of their equilibrium positions are shown as positive on the
graph and particle displacements to the left are shown as negative on the graph.
The period of the wave is T.

the positions of some of the particles of the medium at time $t_{0}$ and a graph showing the
particle displacements at the same time $t_{0}$.
Particle displacements to the right of their equilibrium positions are shown as positive on the
graph and particle displacements to the left are shown as negative on the graph.
The period of the wave is T.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
A longitudinal sound wave is travelling through a solid. The initial intensity of the wave is I_{0}.
The frequency of the wave remains constant and the amplitude falls to half of its original
value.
Determine, in terms of I_{0}, the final intensity of the wave.
intensity = I_{0}
parts.question_text_latex:
A longitudinal sound wave is travelling through a solid. The initial intensity of the wave is $I_{0}$.
The frequency of the wave remains constant and the amplitude falls to half of its original
value.
Determine, in terms of $I_{0}$, the final intensity of the wave.
$intensity = I_{0} $
